title: Invocation Interface Reconciler and Auto-Recovery Playbook
creator: Priya Kothari
description: Design and implement a runtime and orchestration layer that detects invocation interface deltas (structured-output shapes and function-call signatures) during staged rollouts, tries safe automatic reconciliation where feasible, and triggers deterministic rollbacks / mitigation playbooks when incompatibilities affect production callers. The goal is to reduce customer-facing breakages during model upgrades while preserving fast rollouts for low-risk changes.
updates: 2026-02-15 - Priya Kothari: Created ticket. Goal: reduce manual rollback overhead and surface contract diffs earlier in the rollout pipeline.

2026-02-20 - Liam O'Connor: Spike complete. Implemented offline delta scorer that compares previous stable model outputs against candidate on a 5000-sample prompt set (schema fuzz + function signature delta + semantic argument mapping). Scorer produces a single compatibility score (0..100).

2026-02-24 - Liam O'Connor: Decision: use three-tier response handling in runtime: 1) safe passthrough, 2) shim/coerce outputs for known benign deltas (type widening, missing optional fields), 3) hard-fail and increment contract-violation counter for incompatible changes. Pushed proto for shim API (PR #1223).
2026-02-26 - PM review (Ana Ruiz): Prefer conservative defaults for first rollout. Set canary threshold to 1% traffic and require <0.5% contract-violation rate for 30m before moving to 5%.
2026-03-01 - Security (Chen Wu): Confirmed no secret exposure risk from shim. Recommended KMS-backed audit logging for any runtime transformations. Added to scope.

2026-03-01 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented auto-rollback hook that triggers when contract-violation rate > 2% for two consecutive 10-minute windows or when downstream function error rate spikes by >50% relative to baseline.
2026-03-01 - QA (Elena Park): Began end-to-end tests using synthetic tool-call suite and synthetic clients to validate rollback timing and alerting.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility scorer runs in CI for every candidate model and produces a human-readable report (schema diffs, signature deltas, sample-level examples).
Runtime can apply shim/coercion rules for at least two types of benign deltas (optional field addition and numeric type widening) with audit logs enabled.
Shadow traffic pipeline runs candidate models on 5% of sampled requests and surfaces contract-violation rate to the rollout controller dashboard.
Automated rollback triggers fire deterministically under defined thresholds and rollback is observable in the Console with reason and sample examples.
End-to-end tests cover rollback scenarios and confirm no silent data loss (KV cache and streaming sessions preserved) after rollback.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike) - offline scorer and report generation (owner: Liam) - complete
Phase 2 (Runtime) - implement shim API + transformation registry + audit logging (owner: Runtime team, subtask ENG-51431)
Phase 3 (Orchestration) - integrate scorer into CI + shadow traffic pipeline and simple gating rules (owner: Rollouts team, subtask ENG-51432)
Phase 4 (Safety) - auto-rollback hook, alerting, and postmortem automation (owner: SRE, subtask ENG-51433)
Phase 5 (QA/Docs) - run canary exercises, document operator runbook, publish Confluence guide (owner: DX)
risks: False positives from schema-fuzz scoring could block safe rollouts: mitigation = conservative thresholds and manual 'override' for trusted model owners.
Runtime shims may hide regressions if overused: mitigation = auditable transformations and limit to explicitly whitelisted rules with TTL.
Performance overhead on latency-sensitive routes from on-the-fly coercion: mitigation = implement shims in native runtime path and optimize hot paths + sampling rate limits.

Edge-case tool-calls where arguments are reordered or semantically renamed will remain hard-to-automate: mitigation = require developer-supplied migration mapping or maintain backward-compatible model variants.
review_notes: Design review 2026-02-23 (PM Ana Ruiz): Asked for a clear staging progression (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) and explicit cool-down windows between stages.
Security review 2026-02-27 (Chen Wu): Approved but requested KMS-backed transformation logs and RBAC checks for who can create shims.
Runtime review 2026-02-28 (Marco Silva): Suggested pushing heavy validation to background tasks and using a cached compatibility verdict per model-version to avoid repeated expensive checks.
qa_plan: Add compatibility check to pre-release CI that fails on high delta scores (threshold initially set to 85).
Create synthetic clients that exercise function-calls with optional/variant payloads to ensure shims behave correctly.
Perform staged canary runs against internal services with mock downstreams to assert rollback triggers and no lasting state corruption.
postmortem_playbook: On rollback: automatically capture 1k mismatched samples and attach to incident ticket.
Notify owning team with suggested migration steps and automatic link to compatibility report.
Start automated regression run that repros top 20 failures and posts to the incident thread for triage.
If rollout caused user-visible errors: schedule a blameless postmortem within 3 business days and checkpoint a migration plan.
